newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: AIDS figures climb 18 percent globally in year.
newsitem.headline: AIDS figures climb 18 percent globally in year.

text.p: Nearly 1.65 million people have been officially reported as having contracted AIDS since the start of the pandemic, an increase of 18 percent from a year ago, the World Health Organisation (WHO) said on Friday.

But the United Nations health agency, which issued its semi-annual figures reported by its 191 member states, estimated that the actual cumulative number of victims of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS) was closer to 8.4 million.
"As of 30 June 1997, a cumulative total of 1,644,183 AIDS cases in adults and children had been reported to WHO since the onset of the pandemic," WHO said in a weekly bulletin.
This compared with an annual rise of 19 percent recorded at the end of June 1996, according to WHO officials.

But it was not clear whether the one point drop in the annual increase could be attributed to new treatments slowing the onset of AIDS in people who carry the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) or whether it was due to delays in states reporting.
The United States reported the largest number of AIDS cases, 581,429, followed by Brazil with 103,262, Tanzania with 82,174 Thailand with 59,782 and France with 45,395, according to WHO.
